privacy.subtitle: For candidates, employers and website visitors
privacy.notice: Marketing SMS consent is optional and separate from accepting these Terms or registering for free recruitment assistance.

sections.title: About this Privacy Policy
sections.text: This Privacy Policy explains how Jooblie collects, uses, discloses, safeguards and retains personal information in connection with its website, registration forms, candidate screening, employer introductions, recruitment support, employer accounts, communications and optional marketing. It applies to Job Seekers, Employers, employer representatives, website visitors and individuals contacting Jooblie. Jooblie is a recruitment-service division of Clarity Campus / 17617275 Canada Society. For privacy questions or to exercise privacy rights, contact info@jooblie.com or write to 3016 5th Avenue NE, Calgary, Alberta, Canada. This Policy is intended for Canadian operations and is subject to the privacy laws that apply to the activity and individual, including Alberta's Personal Information Protection Act where applicable, the federal Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act where applicable, and any applicable provincial requirements.

sections.title: Privacy principles and accountability
sections.text: Jooblie commits to handling personal information for identified, appropriate and lawful purposes; giving meaningful notice; obtaining consent where required; limiting unnecessary collection; applying reasonable security protections; maintaining accuracy; limiting retention; and supporting access, correction and complaint processes. The organization remains accountable for personal information under its control even when a service provider processes it on its behalf. We will designate an accountable privacy contact and maintain internal practices for access controls, incident response, service-provider oversight and handling individual requests.

sections.title: Who is covered and what roles apply
sections.text: A Job Seeker is an individual seeking employment, referrals, registration or hiring assistance. An Employer is a business or hiring representative using Jooblie to source candidates, advertise positions or manage recruitment. A visitor may browse pages or contact us without creating an account. Jooblie determines how and why it processes the candidate or employer data it collects for its own operations. Employers receiving a candidate application or authorized referral generally make their own decisions about the applicant data they subsequently collect and retain. Where Jooblie processes information strictly under an Employer's written instructions, the parties should separately document their respective responsibilities as required by applicable law.

sections.title: Categories of information we may collect
sections.text: Depending on how you use the Services, information may include: ● Identity and contact information: name, email, telephone number, city, province, preferred contact method and similar details. ● Candidate background: resumes, experience, skills, education, training, professional licences, references you choose to provide, availability, language skills, career preferences and wage expectations. ● Recruitment information: positions applied for, screening answers, matching notes, interview arrangements, employer communications and recruiting outcomes known to Jooblie. ● Work eligibility: work-authorization category and eligibility details reasonably necessary for a specific role; government document copies are not requested for general initial registration unless separately justified and securely collected. ● Employer information: company name, business address, contact details, hiring needs, job descriptions, commercial communications, purchase records and invoice details. ● Technical and usage information: IP address, device/browser details, page interactions, approximate location inferred from technology, cookies or similar identifiers when enabled, and diagnostic logs. ● Communications preferences and consent evidence: the form wording accepted, checked choices, timestamp, source form, mobile number, subscription preferences, unsubscribe records and communications history. ● Safety and compliance records: suspected impersonation, prohibited-fee complaints, abuse reports and information reasonably required for investigation or compliance. We do not ask Job Seekers for their Social Insurance Number, financial account credentials or upfront recruitment payments as a condition of registering or being considered for work.

sections.title: Sources of information
sections.text: We may receive information directly from a registration form, resume, application, telephone call, text, email, meeting, Employer inquiry or support request. Subject to lawful authority, notice and any required consent, we may also receive referral details from Employers, candidate-sourcing services, professional networks, public professional profiles, service providers or a person whom a user has authorized to refer them. Where information comes from another source, we seek to identify its source and the purpose of collecting it and provide required notice. We do not interpret mere public availability on social media as unrestricted permission to collect or market to a person.

sections.title: Purposes for collecting and using information
sections.text: We process information to: ● register users and respond to requests for free recruitment assistance; ● assess qualifications and match candidate preferences to potential vacancies; ● contact Job Seekers about relevant applications, requested introductions, interviews and service questions; ● with lawful authorization, share candidate materials with potential hiring Employers; ● help Employers manage legitimate sourcing, screening and recruitment workflows; ● maintain employer accounts, administer paid Employer Orders, process invoices and respond to billing requests; ● detect fraud, fake listings, unlawful job-placement fees, harassment and misuse; ● administer security, analytics, technical operation and service improvements where lawful; ● maintain required tax, financial, employment-agency, complaint and compliance records; and ● send optional promotional messages only with the consent or other lawful basis required for that particular channel and message. We will not use personal information for materially unrelated purposes without additional notice and consent where required.

sections.title: Candidate matching and disclosures to Employers
sections.text: Submitting a resume or requesting help with a particular opportunity allows Jooblie to assess the information for the stated recruitment purpose. Before sharing a candidate's identifiable resume or profile with an Employer, we will obtain appropriate authorization or consent and provide meaningful notice about the recipient or category of recipients and purpose of disclosure. Relevant details may include work history, qualifications, skills, availability, city, contact information and application materials. We aim to share information proportionate to the position rather than full identity or immigration documents unnecessarily. If a candidate wants their information considered for a wider pool of Employers, Jooblie will identify that broader matching purpose and use an appropriate candidate choice rather than treating ordinary registration as unlimited circulation permission. An Employer may conduct separate interviews, reference checks or onboarding and must provide its own appropriate notices. Information an Employer lawfully receives may be retained by it separately; Jooblie cannot guarantee deletion from every Employer's independently controlled records.

sections.title: Candidate-profile visibility and choices
sections.text: If Jooblie offers a searchable candidate directory or talent pool in the future, we will describe its visibility setting before activation. The default for a Job Seeker's identifiable profile will not be public search-engine publication merely because the person registered. Users may request that Jooblie stop circulating their profile for new introductions, subject to legal and operational limits for prior applications. Where a user changes preferences, we apply the new instruction prospectively. A prior application, email or employer download cannot always be recalled; the recipient Employer is responsible for handling data it has lawfully received.

sections.title: Job-seeker fees and no outcome guarantees
sections.text: Jooblie does not collect personal payment-card information from Job Seekers for job finding, recruitment, referrals, screening, employer introductions or securing employment, because these services are free to Job Seekers. Jooblie does not promise a job, interview, offer, immigration sponsorship, LMIA, work permit or permanent residence in exchange for registration or data submission. These matters are determined by independent Employers and, for immigration decisions, competent government authorities.

sections.title: Employer and payment information
sections.text: Employer account contacts may provide names, company details, work emails, telephone numbers, invoicing instructions and commercial records. When an Employer purchases Paid Services, the payment provider may collect payment-card or bank-payment details directly; Jooblie should receive only the transaction information reasonably needed for invoicing, reconciliation and support unless a different secure arrangement is expressly disclosed. Jooblie may preserve accounting and contracting information as legally required. Candidate information must not be repurposed for employer sales prospecting or unrelated promotional solicitation without the required independent legal basis.

sections.title: Service messages versus promotional communications
sections.text: Jooblie may contact users about a specific registration, application, requested interview, account security matter, order, payment or support inquiry when a lawful basis exists. Those operational communications are different from marketing and promotional campaigns. Whether a particular message is a commercial electronic message depends on its content and applicable law, not merely the label assigned to it. Providing a phone number or agreeing to general website Terms does not itself give express consent to promotional SMS. Consent for marketing is requested separately. Candidates can refuse promotional contact without losing free recruitment help.

sections.title: Promotional SMS/MMS consent and withdrawal
sections.text: Where a user affirmatively selects Jooblie's separate, initially unchecked promotional SMS/MMS checkbox, Jooblie may send texts about job campaigns, hiring events, recruitment opportunities, employer programs, service news and promotional offers at the number provided. Message frequency may vary and standard message and data rates may apply. Marketing consent is optional and is not a condition of registration, recruitment assistance, interviewing or hiring. Users can unsubscribe from promotional text messages at any time by replying STOP to a supported sender or contacting info@jooblie.com. HELP may be used where supported for assistance. Jooblie will honour withdrawal in accordance with law, maintain suppression records to avoid inadvertently resubscribing users, and not share SMS consent with an unrelated Employer for that Employer's independent advertising. An Employer must obtain its own lawful marketing consent if it wishes to send promotional content. We maintain reasonable consent records, which may include the exact disclosure shown, date, time, form or campaign source, mobile number, affirmative action and withdrawal history. We may retain minimal suppression evidence even after promotional contact ends to respect the opt-out and prove compliance.

sections.title: Promotional email and other marketing
sections.text: Where permitted by applicable law, Jooblie may send email newsletters, recruitment-service announcements, hiring campaigns or other commercial electronic messages after obtaining the necessary consent or establishing another lawful basis. Marketing communications will identify the sender and give a straightforward way to unsubscribe. A marketing opt-out will be reflected across relevant Jooblie systems. An opt-out from general promotions does not necessarily cancel a person’s requested application-specific updates, but any further messages will remain subject to applicable anti-spam and privacy law. We will not make a user consent to promotions as the price of free job-seeker assistance.

sections.title: Website analytics, cookies and similar technologies
sections.text: When enabled on the website, cookies, analytics tags or similar technologies may be used for site functionality, security, performance measurement, remembering preferences and evaluating campaigns. These technologies may collect a browser identifier, page interaction, referral URL, approximate location and technical information. Some analytics or advertising providers may receive information as service providers or independent parties depending on configuration. We will provide notices and choices about non-essential tracking when required by applicable law and will not assume every tracking purpose is necessary. Users can also control many cookies through their browser. Blocking certain functional technologies may affect website operation. The precise cookie and tracking inventory should be disclosed in a supplementary cookie notice if such tools are deployed.

sections.title: Service providers and permitted recipients
sections.text: Jooblie may disclose limited personal information to authorized staff, recruitment personnel, Employers selected for a hiring purpose, email and SMS delivery providers, website hosting and storage vendors, customer-management or applicant-tracking vendors, payment processors, security providers, accountants, professional advisers, or competent authorities where appropriate. Service providers must be contractually or otherwise appropriately restricted to authorized processing and reasonable protection measures. We do not sell Job Seeker information or mobile numbers as an unrelated commercial marketing list. We do not provide candidate contact lists to Employers for unrelated advertising.

sections.title: Storage and transfers outside a province or Canada
sections.text: Depending on approved technology vendors and the location of an Employer, information may be stored or accessed outside the province where it was collected or outside Canada. When cross-border processing occurs, foreign laws may in some circumstances permit access by foreign courts, law enforcement or government authorities. Jooblie will assess third-party vendors, use appropriate contractual and technical safeguards, and provide any additional disclosures or assessments required by the relevant provincial law. We do not promise that all information stays exclusively in Canada unless a particular service separately gives that assurance.

sections.title: Data minimization, sensitivity and immigration status
sections.text: We aim to request only information reasonably needed for a particular recruitment purpose. Job Seekers should not include Social Insurance Numbers, bank account numbers, medical diagnoses, unnecessary government identification images or detailed immigration documents in initial public registration forms. If an Employer or authorized professional lawfully needs sensitive information at a later stage, separate notice, lawful authority, secure collection and any needed consent should be provided. Sensitive details will not be used for unlawful employment screening, discriminatory decisions or unrelated marketing. Employers are responsible for their own hiring assessments, lawful accommodation procedures and compliance obligations.

sections.title: Information security and breach response
sections.text: Jooblie will use reasonable safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of data and the risks of unauthorized access, such as access restrictions, staff confidentiality requirements, secure account administration, vendor oversight, appropriate authentication and monitoring of reported concerns. No online platform or electronic transmission can be guaranteed absolutely secure. When an incident involving personal information occurs, we will investigate, contain and document it, and notify affected persons and regulators when required by applicable law. Individuals who suspect fraudulent messages or unauthorized disclosure should contact info@jooblie.com without delay.

sections.title: Data retention and deletion
sections.text: Jooblie retains personal information only for periods reasonably necessary for recruitment activity, user requests, legal and regulatory compliance, resolving complaints, enforcing contracts, preserving accounting records and maintaining a defensible security history. Different categories may require different retention periods. Inactive candidate records should be periodically reviewed and deleted, de-identified or archived only where a lawful reason remains. Users may ask about the relevant retention period for their information or request deletion. Some data may need to be retained for tax, statutory recruitment recordkeeping, fraud-prevention, legal-hold or dispute purposes. Marketing suppression records may be retained to document and respect an unsubscribe request. Any deletion request is assessed against those obligations rather than treated as an absolute promise to erase every record immediately.

sections.title: Access, correction, consent withdrawal and deletion requests
sections.text: Subject to applicable privacy law and lawful exceptions, individuals may ask what personal information Jooblie holds about them, request access, challenge accuracy, request correction, withdraw consent for discretionary uses, object to future candidate-profile sharing and request deletion where appropriate. Requests should be sent to info@jooblie.com and identify the nature of the request. We may take proportionate steps to verify the requester's identity before disclosing information and respond within applicable legal timelines. Withdrawal of consent is generally prospective and may be subject to reasonable notice, contractual consequences and legal restrictions. A Job Seeker can withdraw promotional SMS consent without affecting eligibility for free recruitment services.

sections.title: Employers independent privacy obligations
sections.text: Employers that receive resumes, screening responses, interview notes or other Candidate Data are responsible for maintaining an appropriate privacy notice and lawful collection, use, disclosure, retention, security and access procedures in relation to their own records. An Employer must not use candidate information for non-recruitment promotions without appropriate consent, export data indiscriminately, discriminate unlawfully, or disclose it to unrelated parties. If a candidate asks Jooblie to remove a previously submitted application from an Employer's system, we may assist with identifying the recipient where reasonable, but the Employer independently handles records and requests under its own legal responsibilities.

sections.title: Automated tools and human decisions
sections.text: Jooblie may use limited administrative software to organize profiles, deduplicate records, search for relevant skills or support staff with summaries. If material automated assessment or artificial-intelligence functionality is deployed, we will evaluate the required notices, safeguards and human oversight and will not silently present automated screening as a guaranteed or final employment decision. Employers make their own hiring decisions. A software-generated candidate suggestion is not an assurance that the candidate qualifies for a job, work permit or any legal status.

sections.title: Children and minors
sections.text: The Services are directed primarily to people seeking lawful employment and authorized business representatives. A person below the age at which they can independently provide effective consent in the relevant jurisdiction should not submit personal information without appropriate parent or guardian involvement and a lawful basis. Employers remain responsible for complying with minimum-age employment requirements and additional protections for minors.

sections.title: Complaints and regulatory rights
sections.text: Questions or complaints should be directed to the privacy contact at info@jooblie.com. We aim to examine complaints fairly, explain the relevant practice and correct substantiated errors or gaps. Individuals may also have the right to complain to the privacy regulator with jurisdiction, including the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner of Alberta or the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, depending on the circumstances. This Policy does not limit statutory remedies or regulator jurisdiction.

sections.title: Revisions and contact details
sections.text: We may change this Policy as practices, technologies or laws evolve. The date at the top identifies the version. Material changes affecting how previously collected information is used will be accompanied by additional notice or a fresh consent where required. Privacy and marketing choices remain separate from acceptance of website Terms. Privacy contact: info@jooblie.com. Mailing address: 3016 5th Avenue NE, Calgary, Alberta, Canada. Website: https://www.jooblie.com/. Job-seeker recruitment and employer-connection services remain free of charge to Job Seekers; no placement or immigration outcome is guaranteed.

terms.title: Terms and Conditions
terms.subtitle: For job seekers, employers and website users
terms.notice: Job-finding services are free for Job Seekers. Job placements, offers, work permits and permanent residence are not guaranteed.

sections.title: Introduction, scope and acceptance
sections.text: These Terms and Conditions (the “Terms”) govern access to jooblie.com and any associated registration forms, recruitment programs, communications, employer-facing services and related tools (collectively, the “Services”) provided under the Jooblie brand. “Jooblie,” “we,” “our,” and “us” refer to the operator identified above. “You” means any person or organization using the Services. The Services serve job seekers, employers and authorized employer representatives. Certain provisions expressly apply only to Job Seekers or Employers. By registering, submitting information, posting a role, requesting recruitment support, or otherwise using the Services, you agree to these Terms to the extent a binding acceptance is legally required. Merely viewing publicly available pages does not constitute agreement to optional marketing. An employer's executed proposal, order form or separate recruitment services agreement (“Employer Order”) may establish specific fees, scope, milestones and guarantees. If it conflicts with these Terms, the Employer Order governs only the conflicting commercial subject, except mandatory legal protections and the absolute prohibition on shifting recruitment fees to Job Seekers.

sections.title: Definitions
sections.text: “Job Seeker” means an individual who registers, applies for a job, requests an introduction, or receives recruitment assistance. “Employer” means a business or authorized hiring representative that seeks candidates, posts positions or buys recruitment services. “Job Listing” means a published or shared vacancy or proposed opportunity. “Candidate Data” means a Job Seeker's submitted profile, resume, preferences, responses, communications and related information. “Employer Data” means employer profile details, hiring instructions, job information and account records. “Paid Services” means recruitment, advertising, subscriptions, screening or similar services purchased by an Employer pursuant to an Employer Order. “Applicable Law” includes all relevant employment, recruitment licensing, human rights, privacy, consumer protection, immigration, anti-spam and other laws.

sections.title: Jooblie’s role and nature of the service
sections.text: Jooblie provides employment-connection and recruitment-support services. Depending on the program and jurisdiction, services may include receiving candidate registrations, assessing information supplied by candidates, searching and presenting employer opportunities, coordinating employer introductions, assisting communications, sourcing applicants and supporting employer hiring workflows. Unless an Employer Order states otherwise and applicable law permits, Jooblie is not the employer of any Job Seeker, does not employ candidates on behalf of client employers, and does not exercise the employer's hiring authority. Employers independently decide whom to interview, assess, hire, sponsor, retain or reject. The employment contract, compensation, work location, conditions and statutory employment responsibilities are determined by the Employer and Job Seeker, not Jooblie.

sections.title: Absolutely no recruitment fees to Job Seekers
sections.text: JOB SEEKER RECRUITMENT SERVICES ARE FREE. Jooblie does not charge, collect, require, request or accept any direct or indirect fee from Job Seekers in exchange for job searching, registration, candidate screening, recruitment assistance, employer introductions, interviews, job placement, or securing or attempting to secure employment. No Job Seeker must purchase training, a resume service, immigration service, subscription, deposit, gift card or other item as a condition of receiving Jooblie's job-finding assistance or being considered for a position. Neither an Employer nor a third-party recruiter acting on Jooblie's behalf may charge a candidate or recover employer-paid recruitment costs through a payroll deduction, wage reduction, deposit, reimbursement arrangement, third-party collection, or other indirect means contrary to law. Any person demanding payment in Jooblie's name for employment placement should stop communicating, preserve evidence and report the incident to info@jooblie.com. Jooblie may investigate and refer suspected fraud or illegal recruitment fees to appropriate authorities. This clause does not modify mandatory statutory protections, which prevail.

sections.title: No guarantee of jobs, offers, immigration results or timelines
sections.text: REGISTRATION DOES NOT GUARANTEE EMPLOYMENT. Jooblie does not guarantee that any Job Seeker will receive a referral, application review, interview, employer response, job offer, employment, continued employment, particular salary, particular work location, immigration support, a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA), a work permit, an LMIA-exempt authorization, permanent residence or any immigration outcome. A statement that an Employer may consider supporting a qualified candidate with a work permit or permanent-residence pathway describes only a possible employer decision subject to the candidate's eligibility, the employer's willingness, changing laws and government approval. It is not a promise of sponsorship, approval or a right to work in Canada. Government authorities alone determine applications submitted to them. Job Listings and employer needs may change, close, be withdrawn, or be filled without notice.

sections.title: Eligibility, accounts and information accuracy
sections.text: Users must be legally capable of using the Services and must provide complete, current and truthful information. Job Seekers are responsible for the accuracy of resumes, qualifications, licensing, work-authorization statements, employment history and contact details. An individual must not impersonate another person, fabricate credentials, misstate authorization to work or submit another person's personal information without a lawful basis. Employers must use authorized accounts, keep business information accurate and ensure authorized staff use candidate information only for legitimate recruitment purposes. You are responsible for safeguarding login credentials and promptly notifying Jooblie of suspected unauthorized account access. Jooblie may request verification reasonably needed to prevent fraud and may reject incomplete, deceptive or unsafe registrations.

sections.title: Candidate registration, application and consent to introductions
sections.text: When a Job Seeker asks Jooblie to consider them for opportunities or applies for a specific vacancy, Jooblie may use the information they provide to assess fit, communicate with them and, with appropriate notice and consent, share relevant application materials with the identified Employer or a hiring representative assisting that Employer. Jooblie will not treat a general registration as unlimited permission to publish a resume publicly or provide it indiscriminately to every Employer. Where Jooblie offers broader candidate-pool matching, the Job Seeker must be informed about the nature of the sharing and have an appropriate choice or consent mechanism before broader disclosure. Once a candidate has applied to an Employer or authorized sharing, that Employer may independently retain and use the application under its own lawful recruitment practices and privacy notice. A request to Jooblie to delete its copy may not delete records already lawfully held by an Employer.

sections.title: Job Listings, independent verification and safety
sections.text: Job Listings and employer statements may originate from third parties. Jooblie may perform reasonable checks but does not represent that every Job Listing is current, error-free or suitable for every candidate. Candidates should independently verify employer identity, compensation, location, working conditions and required credentials before accepting an offer or providing sensitive documents. Job Seekers must not send Social Insurance Numbers, banking credentials, original identity documents, passport copies or payments to unverified parties based solely on a text, social media message or Job Listing. Legitimate recruitment through Jooblie does not require a placement payment. Employers must promptly correct or withdraw inaccurate or filled positions.

sections.title: Employer representations and posting obligations
sections.text: Each Employer represents and warrants that it is a legitimate hiring organization or duly authorized recruiting representative; has the right to recruit for advertised roles; provides materially accurate job, wage, location, eligibility and workplace information; and will comply with applicable employment standards, human rights, occupational health and safety, immigration, recruiter-licensing, foreign-worker protection and privacy laws. Employers must not advertise fictitious positions, solicit prohibited candidate payments, misrepresent sponsorship availability, seek unlawful discriminatory information, retaliate against candidates exercising statutory rights, harvest candidate data, or use candidates' details for unrelated sales or solicitation. Employers must secure any approvals, recruiter licences, registrations or authorizations applicable to their activities, and may not assume that listing a vacancy on Jooblie makes the hiring process compliant.

sections.title: Foreign-worker recruitment and immigration-related statements
sections.text: Recruitment and immigration are distinct activities. Jooblie does not, merely by offering a candidate introduction, provide regulated immigration legal advice, act as the candidate's authorized immigration representative, or submit immigration applications. Any regulated advice or representation must be provided by a professional legally authorized for that work under a separate, properly disclosed arrangement where applicable. An Employer considering an LMIA, LMIA-exempt employer-specific work permit, or permanent-residence pathway is responsible for its eligibility, employer compliance, accurate statements, lawful fees and duties toward workers. Employers must not pass prohibited recruitment costs to foreign nationals, recover them by deductions or arrange payment through another entity. No Employer may describe a government decision as certain or sell a job offer through the Services.

sections.title: Employer selection, hiring and employment relationship
sections.text: Employers alone are responsible for independent and lawful hiring decisions, background and reference checks conducted with required notices and consents, worker classification, pay, benefits, accessibility accommodations, onboarding, workplace safety, immigration employer compliance and employment agreements. Jooblie may coordinate interviews but is not a party to any resulting employment contract unless expressly agreed in a signed document. Job Seekers are responsible for evaluating offers and complying with lawful requirements. Jooblie is not responsible for a third party's independent hiring decision, failure to respond, delayed start, workplace dispute or termination, except to the extent legal responsibility arises from Jooblie's own conduct and cannot lawfully be excluded.

sections.title: Employer Paid Services and order terms
sections.text: Only Employers may be charged for recruitment, sourcing, screening, advertising, subscriptions or other business services expressly included in an accepted Employer Order or lawful invoice. Pricing, currency, taxes, deliverables, start date, term, renewal, cancellation method and any placement or replacement commitment must be stated before purchase. Unless expressly included in a signed order, Jooblie does not promise a minimum number of candidates, qualified applicants, interviews, hires or hiring timelines. Requests exceeding agreed scope may require a new written quote. The Employer Refund Policy governs cancellations and refunds of Paid Services subject to the terms of an Employer Order and non-excludable law. Employers remain solely responsible for their payment obligations; charges must not be shifted to Job Seekers.

sections.title: Communications and appointment coordination
sections.text: Jooblie may communicate about a requested registration, application, interview, service issue, account security or Employer Order by email, phone or other channels reasonably related to the service. The type and legal basis of each communication will be assessed under applicable communications and privacy law. Opting out of marketing does not necessarily prevent essential account or application messages that are lawful to send. If Jooblie enables messaging or calendar integrations, participants must use them lawfully and respectfully, verify meeting details directly when important, and refrain from harassment, threats or unsolicited commercial contact with candidates. Delivery of email, SMS or calendar invitations may be delayed or interrupted.

sections.title: Marketing, promotional SMS and electronic-message consent
sections.text: Jooblie does not treat registration, submission of a phone number, acceptance of these Terms or an employment inquiry as automatic express consent to marketing. Where Jooblie requests express permission for promotional SMS or MMS, the request must appear as a separate, voluntary and unchecked opt-in identifying Jooblie, the purpose of messages, contact information and the ability to withdraw. If you affirmatively opt in, promotional texts may include job opportunity campaigns, hiring events, employer opportunities, recruitment news, service promotions and offers. Frequency may vary; standard message and data rates may apply. You may withdraw at any time by replying STOP where supported or emailing info@jooblie.com. Reply HELP where supported for assistance. Marketing consent is not required to register or obtain free job-seeker support, and declining it will not affect eligibility for the Services. Jooblie will record consent and withdrawal, honour unsubscribe requests within applicable legal periods, and include required identification and unsubscribe instructions in commercial electronic messages. Consent to messages from Jooblie does not authorize unrelated Employers to send promotional messages. A Job Seeker's consent to share a resume for recruitment is separate from consent to marketing.

sections.title: Privacy and confidential information
sections.text: Jooblie processes personal information according to its Privacy Policy and applicable law. Employers receiving Candidate Data must protect it, restrict access to personnel involved in recruitment, use it only for authorized hiring purposes, respect candidate rights and retain it no longer than lawful and necessary. Employers must not resell candidate lists, use details for unrelated marketing without independent lawful consent, or disclose a candidate's information to unrelated parties. Users must also protect nonpublic commercial terms, confidential employer instructions and any nonpublic Job Seeker information obtained through the Services, except where disclosure is authorized, reasonably necessary to perform the Services, or required by law.

sections.title: Prohibited conduct and anti-fraud rules
sections.text: You must not engage in fraud, impersonation, phishing, misleading sponsorship advertising, unlawful discrimination, sexual harassment, trafficking, coercion, unlawful fees, spam, security circumvention, scraping at scale, reverse engineering, introduction of malicious code, false reviews, exploitation of candidate information, or activity that infringes others' rights. Jooblie may investigate complaints, preserve relevant information as lawfully permitted, suspend or remove content or accounts, and cooperate with authorities as required. Jooblie may decline to work with any Employer who requests unlawful recruitment practices or appears to require prohibited worker payments.

sections.title: Content, intellectual property and permitted use
sections.text: The Jooblie brand, website layout, original platform content and associated materials are owned by Jooblie or their respective licensors. Users receive a limited, revocable, non-exclusive permission to access the Services for legitimate employment and recruitment purposes. They may not resell, scrape, reproduce, or commercially exploit platform information outside these purposes without written permission. Users retain ownership of their lawful submissions. They grant Jooblie a limited, non-exclusive licence to host, process, format and communicate submitted materials only as reasonably needed to provide and improve the requested Services, subject to privacy choices and applicable law. This licence does not authorize sale of Candidate Data for unrelated purposes.

sections.title: External services, availability and changes
sections.text: The Services may contain links to third-party sites, job application systems, payment processors or communication platforms governed by their own terms and notices. Jooblie cannot control independent third-party practices. Platform functions, eligibility criteria and recruitment workflows may change to reflect business requirements, security, compliance or technological availability. Jooblie aims for reasonable service availability but does not guarantee uninterrupted access, error-free integrations or delivery of every electronic submission. Users should keep their own copies of important information and contact Jooblie if a material communication does not arrive.

sections.title: Suspension and termination
sections.text: A Job Seeker may stop using the Services and request closure or data-related action in accordance with the Privacy Policy. Jooblie may suspend or terminate accounts for material Terms breaches, security threats, illegal conduct, fraudulent recruitment activity, unlawful fees, abusive behaviour or other legitimate reasons, subject to applicable law. Employer Orders remain governed by their express terms and the Employer Refund Policy. Closing an account does not erase accrued lawful fees, confidentiality obligations, privacy responsibilities, rights relating to completed services or legally required records.

sections.title: Disclaimers and allocation of risk
sections.text: To the fullest extent permitted by law, the Services are provided on an “as available” basis without any promise of a specific hiring result, candidate volume, processing time, sponsorship decision or government approval. Jooblie does not warrant the truth of independent third-party statements, although it may take reasonable steps to address reported issues. Nothing in these Terms excludes liability or rights that cannot lawfully be excluded, including obligations arising from fraud, wilful misconduct, mandatory privacy or employment law, or applicable statutory remedies. A User remains responsible for their own unlawful acts and for independently evaluating information on which they act.

sections.title: Liability and employer responsibility
sections.text: Subject to non-excludable law, Jooblie is not liable for indirect or consequential commercial losses, anticipated hiring savings, lost profits or lost business opportunities resulting from a third party's hiring decisions or from candidate withdrawal. Any contractual monetary cap for a specific Employer's Paid Services, if applicable, must be addressed in the signed Employer Order and cannot nullify mandatory legal rights. An Employer is responsible for claims and losses arising from its unlawful job advertisements, prohibited candidate fees, misuse of personal information, discrimination, workplace obligations, breach of representations or instructions that violate law. The parties will cooperate reasonably in resolving bona fide complaints and mitigating foreseeable loss. No indemnity requires a party to compensate the other for that other party's own fraud or wilful misconduct.

sections.title: Governing law and disputes
sections.text: Subject to mandatory provincial, federal and local laws, these Terms are governed by the laws of Alberta and applicable federal laws of Canada. Courts with jurisdiction in Alberta may hear contractual disputes, without preventing individuals or regulators from using statutory complaint processes or mandatory local forums to which they are entitled. Before commencing a commercial contractual dispute, an Employer should provide written details to info@jooblie.com and allow a reasonable opportunity for a good-faith resolution. Nothing in this clause restricts urgent legal relief, statutory limitation periods, worker rights, privacy complaints or regulatory reporting.

sections.title: Updates, severability and interpretation
sections.text: Jooblie may revise these Terms to reflect legal, operational or service changes. The effective date will be updated, and notice of material changes will be given when required by law or reasonably appropriate. Changes will not retroactively alter a signed Employer Order without legal basis or agreement. If part of these Terms is invalid, the remainder continues to apply so far as lawful. A failure to enforce one provision does not waive other rights.

sections.title: Contact and reporting concerns
sections.text: For recruitment-fee concerns, suspected fake job offers, questions about these Terms, candidate complaints, Employer billing disputes or requests for assistance, email info@jooblie.com. Mailing location: 3016 5th Avenue NE, Calgary, Alberta, Canada. Website: https://www.jooblie.com/. For personal-information requests, see the Privacy Policy. Job Seekers are never required to pay for job-placement support.

refund.title: Employer Refund and Cancellation Policy
refund.subtitle: For employer-paid recruitment and business services only
refund.notice: Employer fees must never be charged to, deducted from, or recovered from Job Seekers. No hire or immigration approval is guaranteed.

sections.title: Purpose and scope
sections.text: This Employer Refund and Cancellation Policy (the “Refund Policy”) describes when Jooblie may issue refunds, credits or fee adjustments for paid business-to-business recruitment, advertising, subscriptions, candidate sourcing, screening and related services purchased by Employers. It applies only to amounts actually paid to Jooblie by an Employer under a lawful invoice or accepted written Employer Order. JOB SEEKERS ARE NEVER CHARGED RECRUITMENT OR JOB-PLACEMENT FEES. Accordingly, there are no candidate placement fees to refund. No Employer may pass or recover Jooblie's recruitment charges from a Job Seeker, directly or indirectly, contrary to law.

sections.title: Relationship to an Employer Order
sections.text: An accepted proposal, statement of work, subscription order or written recruitment agreement may specify a service term, deliverables, payment event, earned-fee criteria, a replacement guarantee or distinct refund conditions. Those express commercial terms govern the corresponding purchase to the extent lawful. If no provision in the Employer Order addresses a refund issue, this Refund Policy applies. The commercial scope must be identified in writing before payment. A general promise to “find candidates” without a defined service or placement-fee trigger will not be interpreted as a guarantee of a hire.

sections.title: Definitions and commencement
sections.text: “Service Commencement” occurs when Jooblie begins a paid activity authorized by the Employer, such as launching advertising, creating and publishing a paid Job Listing, conducting a planned search, performing candidate screening or beginning a subscription term. “Earned Fees” are charges fairly attributable to services actually delivered, documented work completed or agreed milestones reached. “Unperformed Services” are prepaid, severable deliverables or service periods not yet provided. A “Placement Fee” is a fee payable on the objective event stated in a written Employer Order, such as a candidate's accepted offer or actual employment start. No placement-fee trigger is implied merely because an introduction occurs.

sections.title: Fundamental allocation of risk
sections.text: Jooblie will undertake the specific activities agreed in an Employer Order using reasonable care, but does not guarantee a minimum number of responses, interviews, successful hires, employee retention, LMIAs, work permits, permanent residence approvals or timing of government decisions unless a lawful, narrow and explicit written service commitment states otherwise. An Employer's dissatisfaction with an independently made hiring decision, a Job Seeker's refusal or withdrawal, a government refusal, or changed labour-market conditions does not by itself mean that properly delivered services are refundable. Conversely, a clause describing services as non-refundable does not allow Jooblie to keep money for demonstrably unperformed services where law, a written agreement or Jooblie's own material breach requires a refund.

sections.title: Refund rules by type of paid service
sections.text: A. Candidate-sourcing or screening projects. If an Employer cancels before material work begins, prepaid fees for unstarted work are generally refundable, less only agreed and demonstrably incurred non-recoverable third-party charges disclosed before purchase. After commencement, Jooblie may retain the reasonable amount attributable to completed work or achieved milestones; the remaining prepaid amount attributable to undelivered, severable services will be refunded or credited as agreed. B. Job advertising and paid postings. If the campaign has not launched, the prepaid campaign fee is generally refundable after deduction of any disclosed, non-recoverable, authorized costs already incurred. Once published, charges attributable to advertising delivered or the active period already elapsed are earned. If Jooblie itself materially fails to deliver the paid publication period and cannot remedy the failure, the Employer may receive a proportionate refund for the unprovided period, subject to non-excludable rights. C. Recurring subscriptions. A monthly subscription can be cancelled for future billing before its next renewal as described in the Employer Order. Fees for an active month in which access or services were made available are ordinarily earned; a refund or credit may be appropriate for material non-delivery or billing error. For prepaid annual or multi-month services, Jooblie will assess unused full service periods, agreed minimum commitments, disclosed discounts and services already performed, and provide a proportionate refund where required by the Order or law. D. Recruitment/placement or success fees. A placement fee becomes payable only upon the placement event specified in the Employer Order. The Order must clearly state any candidate-replacement window, retention condition or limited guarantee. In the absence of such an express provision, an otherwise earned placement fee is not automatically reversed merely because a hired worker later resigns, is dismissed, or is unable to commence due to an independently determined legal or immigration issue. E. Setup, onboarding or bespoke work. Fees tied to completed setup, account configuration or delivered custom work are earned once the agreed work is provided. Deposits or advances designated for unperformed, severable work are evaluated proportionately rather than automatically forfeited.

sections.title: Cancellation before work begins
sections.text: An Employer wishing to cancel must send written notice to info@jooblie.com identifying its organization, invoice or Order, the service and requested effective date. Jooblie will confirm whether work has begun and identify any authorized, disclosed third-party costs that cannot reasonably be recovered. If the service was not commenced and no disclosed non-recoverable costs were incurred, Jooblie will generally refund the prepaid service fee in full. The cancellation date is the date Jooblie receives a clear notice by an authorized Employer representative, subject to any agreed written notice period for recurring contracts.

sections.title: Cancellation after partial performance
sections.text: For projects with severable milestones or service periods, Jooblie will provide an itemized explanation of work performed, earned fees, committed non-recoverable costs if permitted, and the unused balance. Any refund due will be calculated on the contract's objective pricing or milestone method; absent one, Jooblie will use a reasonable and documented allocation rather than an arbitrary forfeiture. If the Employer obstructs the work by withholding role details, failing to provide approvals or withdrawing a vacancy, Jooblie may retain fees for completed services and reasonable, disclosed committed work, subject to the Order and applicable law. No candidate is liable for Employer cancellation costs.

sections.title: Jooblie non-delivery, duplicate billing and corrections
sections.text: If Jooblie materially fails to provide an agreed paid service and does not cure the failure within a reasonable opportunity after notice, the Employer may request an appropriate re-performance, service credit or refund of the affected undelivered portion, subject to the contract and statutory remedies. Confirmed duplicate charges, overpayments and demonstrable invoice errors will be corrected and refunded or credited as applicable. Disputes about the quality of a service will be assessed against the written scope and evidence of delivery; a failure to achieve an outcome not promised in that scope is not itself a service failure.

sections.title: No guarantee of hiring or immigration outcomes
sections.text: Neither payment by an Employer nor an accepted recruitment assignment constitutes a guarantee that a vacancy will be filled, that a Job Seeker will attend an interview, that a candidate will accept or remain in employment, or that a person will receive an LMIA, LMIA-exempt work permit, work authorization, permanent residence or other government approval. Fees for completed lawful recruitment services are not refundable solely because the Employer decides not to hire a candidate, a candidate refuses an offer, government rules change, or a government application is refused or delayed. Any separately contracted lawful guarantee will be applied strictly according to its stated eligibility criteria and remedy.

sections.title: Employer compliance and prohibited fees
sections.text: Employers are responsible for lawful job advertisements, employment standards, anti-discrimination obligations, foreign-worker protections, recruiter licensing and accuracy of sponsorship statements. If an Employer requests illegal fees, fabricated jobs, improper wage deductions, false immigration representations or other prohibited conduct, Jooblie may suspend or cancel the Services and cooperate with enforcement authorities as required. Fees for completed lawful work may remain payable; funds attributable to undelivered work will be addressed under this Policy and law. No refund calculation or contractual term authorizes a worker to be charged any recruitment-related fee.

sections.title: Taxes, processing fees and credits
sections.text: Fees are normally quoted and invoiced in Canadian dollars unless expressly agreed otherwise. Applicable GST/HST or other taxes will be handled under tax law. A refund will include or adjust corresponding taxes as required. Payment-processing costs or third-party charges may be deducted only to the extent separately disclosed before purchase, actually incurred, non-recoverable and lawfully chargeable to the Employer. A credit may be offered as an alternative to a cash refund only where the Employer freely accepts it or a lawful written Order provides for it. Jooblie will not impose a credit instead of a cash refund that the Employer is legally entitled to receive.

sections.title: Refund request procedure and review
sections.text: An authorized Employer representative should email info@jooblie.com with the legal business name, invoice number, amount paid, payment date, relevant service, reason for the request and supporting correspondence. Jooblie may seek additional records necessary to determine work performed and charges earned. Jooblie aims to acknowledge a complete request within five business days and provide a written decision or meaningful status update within fifteen business days, although complex investigations may require more time. An approved refund will be initiated without unreasonable delay to the original payment method where practicable; financial institutions and payment providers may require additional processing time. These target periods do not displace statutory requirements.

sections.title: Chargebacks and billing disputes
sections.text: Employers should first report apparent billing errors to Jooblie so the matter can be investigated and resolved efficiently. This does not waive any lawful payment-card dispute or chargeback right. Jooblie may provide the payment provider with records reasonably needed to establish an authorized charge and services delivered, while protecting Candidate Data and complying with privacy law. Fraudulent or abusive chargeback activity may result in temporary suspension of optional commercial services, but will not affect a Job Seeker's right to free job-finding assistance.

sections.title: Renewal and change of scope
sections.text: A recurring Employer Order must identify its renewal cycle, pricing and cancellation procedure. Employers should give notice before the next renewal date to avoid a new billing period. Material changes in scope, pricing, placement-fee triggers or guarantees require appropriate written acceptance. A conversation or informal advertisement does not silently amend a signed Order. If Jooblie discontinues a prepaid service before the end of the paid term for reasons not attributable to Employer misconduct, it will address the unprovided portion with an appropriate refund or agreed alternative consistent with law.

sections.title: Statutory rights, revisions and contact
sections.text: Nothing in this Policy excludes remedies that cannot lawfully be excluded, including those arising from a material contractual breach, applicable business, tax, fraud or consumer protection legislation or other mandatory rules. If any section conflicts with such law, that law prevails to the extent required. Jooblie may update this Policy for future purchases by updating the effective date and providing notice where required. Existing signed Employer Orders will not be changed retroactively without lawful authority or consent. Refunds and cancellation enquiries: info@jooblie.com. Jooblie: 3016 5th Avenue NE, Calgary, Alberta, Canada. Website: https://www.jooblie.com/. Job Seekers never pay Jooblie to find or secure employment.
